6
A ball is held above the ground and released. It falls to the ground and bounces several times.
The graph shows the variation with time t of the velocity v of the ball.
Q
v
S
t
P
0
0
R
Four points on the graph are labelled P, Q, R and S.
Which statement is not correct?
A
The area under line PQ represents the initial height of the ball.
B
The collisions of the ball with the ground are inelastic.
C
The gradient of the line RS represents the acceleration due to free fall.
D
The maximum upwards velocity of the ball is reached at point P.

hints: Look at the vertical jump from Q to R at the first bounce and compare the size of $v$ at Q just before impact with $v$ at R just after impact.
Recall what area under a $v$-$t$ graph and gradient of a $v$-$t$ graph represent for the falling section OQ and the in-air section RS.
Check the sign for upward motion on this graph where downward is positive, and see where $v$ is most negative compared with point P on the first fall.
walkthrough: Take downward as positive $v$ on this graph. The ball is released from rest, so $v$ grows positively along OQ to the first impact at Q.
Area under $v$-$t$ is displacement $s = \int v \, dt$. The area under OQ to time of Q is the fall distance from release to ground, so it equals the initial height.

At impact the velocity reverses sharply from Q positive to R negative. The upward direction is negative $v$, and $|v_R| < |v_Q|$, so speed and kinetic energy are lost. The bounce is inelastic and later S peaks are lower.

Between bounces the ball is in free fall, so the $v$-$t$ gradient $a = \Delta v / \Delta t$ equals acceleration due to gravity. Line RS is the motion just after the first bounce, so its gradient represents $g$.

Maximum upward velocity means maximum speed in the negative $v$ direction. That occurs just after the bounce at R where $v$ is most negative, not at P which is still part of the first downward fall near $v = 0$. So statement D is not correct. This is option D.

A.explanation: Area under a $v$-$t$ graph is displacement. The area from release to first impact at Q is the distance fallen, which is the initial height.

B.explanation: The rebound speed magnitude at R is smaller than the impact speed magnitude at Q, and later peaks get smaller, so kinetic energy is lost at each bounce.

C.explanation: While in the air on RS the only acceleration is $g$. Gradient of a $v$-$t$ graph is acceleration, so gradient of RS is free-fall acceleration.

D.explanation: Point P is early in the first fall with small downward velocity. Maximum upward velocity is the largest velocity in the upward direction, just after the first bounce at R.
